t:
(a) None of the income retained in the Department of Justice Working Capital Fund pursuant to title I of Public Law 102–140 (105 Stat. 784; 28 U.S.C. 527 note) shall be available for obligation during fiscal year 2013. 
    (b) Not to exceed $30,000,000 of the unobligated balances transferred to the capital account of the Department of Justice Working Capital Fund pursuant to title I of Public Law 102–140 (105 Stat. 
784; 28 U.S.C. 527 note) shall be available for obligation in fiscal year 2013, and any use, obligation, transfer or allocation of such funds shall be treated as a reprogramming of funds under section 505 of this Act. 
    (c) Not to exceed $10,000,000 of the excess unobligated balances available under section 524(c)(8)(E) of title 28, United States Code, shall be available for obligation during fiscal year 2013, and any use, obligation, transfer or allocation of such funds shall be treated as a reprogramming of funds under section 505 of this Act. 
    (d) Of amounts available in the Assets Forfeiture Fund in fiscal year 2013, $154,700,000 shall be for payments associated with joint law enforcement operations as authorized by section 524(c)(1)(I) of title 28, United States Code. 
    (e) The Attorney General shall submit a spending plan to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate not later than 45 days after the date of enactment of this Act detailing the planned distribution of Assets Forfeiture Fund joint law enforcement operations funding during fiscal year 2013. 
    (f) Subsections (a) through (d) of this section shall sunset on September 30, 2013.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the spending plan submission and the reprogramming treatment are procedural consultation, or that "joint law enforcement operations" implies coordination with state and local agencies. The plan goes only to congressional appropriations committees, which are inside the federal government, and the joint-operations language merely earmarks funds for payments. Nothing in the section requires consulting outside parties, public comment, rulemaking, an advisory body, or a right to sue.
fable.s: The Attorney General shall submit a spending plan to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate

opus.w: This section only sets how much money is available from Department of Justice funds and requires a spending plan to be sent to the House and Senate Appropriations Committees. Reports to Congress stay inside the federal government. The tempting reading treats 'joint law enforcement operations' as coordination with state or local agencies, but that phrase just describes what the payments are for. No outside party is consulted before a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue.
opus.s: The Attorney General shall submit a spending plan to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate not later than 45 days after the date of enactment of this Act
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The section refers to "joint law enforcement operations," which usually include state and local police. It also requires a spending plan to be submitted, and reprogrammings (which under section 505 typically require notice to the Appropriations Committees). Those look like outside coordination or a formal review step.
2. **Why it fails:** The joint-operations language only sets aside money. It requires no consultation with state or local agencies before any federal decision. The spending plan and any reprogramming notices go to congressional committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. Nothing here brings in anyone outside the government.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Attorney General to submit a report to Congressional committees. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, so reporting to them is not participation. There is no requirement to consult or coordinate with any outside parties such as states, tribes, or the public.
qwen_chat.s: The Attorney General shall submit a spending plan to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate not later than 45 days after the date of enactment of this Act detailing the planned distribution of Assets Forfeiture Fund joint law enforcement operations funding during fiscal year 2013.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that subsection (e) requires the Attorney General to submit a spending plan to Congressional committees, which sounds like a procedural interaction. However, the definition explicitly states that reports to Congress, its committees, or its members are "inside the federal government" and thus do not constitute participation. The interaction is purely intra-governmental (Executive branch reporting to Legislative branch). There is no consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other outside entities.
